name: Rental vacancy rate
definition: Net rental vacancy rate: vacant units available for rent (not dilapidated) as a share of those units plus renter-occupied units, from the New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey, which is taken about every three years.

source.name: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development / U.S. Census Bureau, New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey, Selected Initial Findings reports (1996-2023)

method: Each value was read from the text of an official HVS findings report downloaded and parsed by this script; the series is only survey years (no interpolation). Value and source document per year: 1984: 2.04% (HPD, 1996 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey report summary, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/1996%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 1987: 2.46% (HPD, 1996 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey report summary, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/1996%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 1991: 3.78% (HPD, 1996 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey report summary, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/1996%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 1993: 3.44% (HPD, 1996 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey report summary, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/1996%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 1996: 4.01% (HPD, 1996 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey report summary, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/1996%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 1999: 3.19% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 1999 NYCHVS, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/1999%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 2002: 2.94% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 2002 NYCHVS, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2002%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 2005: 3.09% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 2005 NYCHVS, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2005%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 2008: 2.88% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 2008 NYCHVS (Feb. 10, 2009), https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2008%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 2011: 3.12% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 2011 NYCHVS (Feb. 9, 2012), https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2011%20NYCHVS%20Selected%20Initial%20Findings.pdf); 2014: 3.45% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 2017 NYCHVS (Feb. 9, 2018), https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2017-hvs-initial-findings.pdf); 2017: 3.63% (HPD, Selected Initial Findings of the 2017 NYCHVS (Feb. 9, 2018), https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2017-hvs-initial-findings.pdf); 2021: 4.54% (HPD, 2023 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey Selected Initial Findings, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2023-nychvs-selected-initial-findings.pdf); 2023: 1.41% (HPD, 2023 New York City Housing and Vacancy Survey Selected Initial Findings, https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hpd/downloads/pdfs/about/2023-nychvs-selected-initial-findings.pdf). 2021 and 2023 margins are half the 90% confidence intervals published in Table 9 of the 2023 report. Earlier reports publish a standard error instead (2005: 0.19, 2008: 0.16, 2011: 0.17, 2017: 0.22 percentage points); those years carry moe = null.
caveats: Survey years only, about every three years; there is no value for the years in between. There was no 2020 survey; the cycle after 2017 was 2021.
The rate is a sample-survey estimate. The 2023 value has a 90% confidence interval of about plus or minus 0.26 points.

Survey design changes affect comparisons: the 2011 report says its results should not be compared directly with 2008 and earlier because the 2011 sample was drawn from the 2010 census and weighted to it, and the 2023 report warns that changes between cycles, including the 2021 cycle, may affect comparability over time.
A rate below 5 percent legally sustains the housing emergency that keeps rent stabilization in force.
The 2026 survey's results are expected in early 2027.
No peer comparison: the survey covers New York City only.
